stories.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.summary: CISA added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2026-133968 (Project MONAI MONAI Label Path Traversal) and CVE-2026-134624 (N-able Mail Assure SSRF).
stories.fix: Organizations should apply available patches and monitor for exploitation, with FCEB agencies required to remediate high-risk KEV vulnerabilities on exposed assets promptly.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
stories.summary: CISA added 10 security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including five Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133311, CVE-2026-133323, CVE-2026-133324) affecting versions 10.3 and earlier that allow arbitrary file upload, XML injection, unauthorized access, command injection, and authentication bypass within the AWV component. Also added are CVE-2026-133469 in Vates Xen Orchestra and CVE-2026-103406 in HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor/Router, both with CVSS 9.8, plus three Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series flaws (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2025-41450) involving path traversal, command injection, and authentication bypass exposing sensitive data.
stories.fix: Mitel provides patch 10.3.0.18 for release 10.3 and recommends upgrading to a later release or restricting external access to the AWV component; Vates and Juniper advise applying their respective fixes, and Danfoss recommends limiting remote access via VPN, configuring Strict mode, and using strong passwords until updates are available.

stories.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
stories.summary: Stolen credentials exposed customer data at Todoist, where an attacker used a compromised version-control credential to access source code, employee accounts, and cloud infrastructure, affecting 6% of users. A new ransomware group called BYOD disrupted at least nine organizations in October–November 2026, causing ambulance diversions, clinic closures, and device shutdowns through credential compromise and a remote access trojan. More than 10 million exposed NGINX services running HTTP/2 are vulnerable to NGINX2Root, allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to corrupt memory and achieve code execution when ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Fix: Customers should update NGINX to a patched version and disable HTTP/2 or restrict access until a fix is applied.

stories.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing ‘Personal and Business Information’
stories.summary: FIFA confirmed it was victim of a cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information. FIFA stated it is working with relevant authorities and law enforcement in response to the incident. A hacking group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claimed responsibility by posting files on social media and later taking credit for leaking over 12 gigabytes of internal documents.

stories.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
stories.summary: North Korea-linked PolinRider campaign has planted a Python loader in over 7,600 GitHub repositories, which reads Ethereum wallet transaction data to decode and execute JavaScript malware that fetches command-and-control server addresses and delivers infostealer payloads. The loader spreads by hijacking maintainer accounts, rewriting commits with hidden build-config entries, and triggering when developers run builds or open projects in VS Code, with the wallet address "0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3" reused across multiple attack waves. Fix: Security researchers recommend verifying maintainer account integrity, auditing Git history for unauthorized force-pushes, and monitoring Ethereum wallet transactions linked to repository loads for suspicious decoder activity.

stories.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
stories.summary: 1Password disclosed a security incident where an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account, used it to access backend systems, and downloaded limited customer account information including names, email addresses, account identifiers, public keys, and Secure Remote Password protocol parameters. The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to the CI/CD system, but 1Password confirmed that no customer vault secrets, passwords, or encryption keys were accessed or compromised. Fix: 1Password disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, hardened GitHub CI/CD and endpoint controls, restored clean versions of the affected service, rotated internal credentials, and lengthened codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

stories.title: 1Password Breach Exposes Customer Data, Internal Source Code
stories.summary: 1Password breach revealed that a hacker stole customer data and source code after compromising an employee's corporate GitHub account, deploying malicious code to backend services and exfiltrating records containing names, emails, account identifiers, public cryptographic keys, authentication parameters, and metadata. The attacker also accessed private source code and the CI/CD system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials, while obtaining tokens from invitation and recovery emails; 1Password confirmed customer vaults and cryptographic keys protecting them were not compromised. In response, the company disabled the compromised GitHub account, invalidated the stolen token, replaced potentially compromised infrastructure credentials, and restored clean versions of affected services.
